params.body:
The same blind spot as the 419 of this morning, and this afternoon it cost another few hours.

Ilse reported a 404 on "meerdere wagens verwijderen" for a dealer she is closing down. Nightwatch held nothing, because Laravel keeps every `HttpException` out of reporting. So the one fact that settles it — WHICH url was missing — could not be retrieved, and four code paths had to be read instead of one log line. The module toggle she also reported was measured end to end on production and answers 200, so that one is not broken; without a trace there was no way to tell those two apart except by hand.

A 404 that a signed-in user hits now leaves a line: who, which method and path, the query string, where they came from, which Livewire method was called, and whether a delegation was active.

A 404 from someone not signed in is deliberately not written. The open side of the platform is full of scanners knocking on /wp-admin and /.env; a log that fills with those is a log nobody reads, which is exactly how this blindness starts. The test pins both halves.

Nothing changes for the visitor. New rule R P2-11.10, next to R P2-11.9 which does the same for a 419.
params.title: A page that is not there says which
